title: Disjointness of Hamming balls at minimum distance
statement: Let $C$ be a code of length $n$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ whose minimum Hamming distance is $d$, and suppose $d > 0$. Write $t = \left\lfloor \frac{d-1}{2} \right\rfloor$. Then for any two distinct codewords $c_1, c_2 \in C$, the Hamming balls $B_t(c_1)$ and $B_t(c_2)$ of radius $t$ centered at $c_1$ and $c_2$ are disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: C is a code of length n over alpha
d is the minimum Hamming distance of C (distance C d)
c_1 and c_2 are codewords in C
replaced: Reformulation of the previous lemma as \texttt{Finset.Disjoint}.
